toc.name: Emergency Shelter
toc.source_toolkit: S&S outcome monitoring toolkits - Emergency Shelter.docx
toc.note: Outcome indicators only. Mandatory indicators encoded for the 2026 TOC. Fixed/locked fields are global and must not be edited by a country office; the 'parameters' array holds the country-defined variables.

global_rules.reporting: Report in GORS for each corresponding project. GORS must be filled within two weeks of data collection, and no later than the 15th of the month following data collection.
global_rules.percentage_calc_note: When reporting in GORS, the percentage is calculated automatically from the numerator and denominator. To calculate manually: 100 * numerator / denominator.
global_rules.baseline_default: No baseline is required for these outcome indicators, and it is recommended not to conduct one - it is not likely to be appropriate.
global_rules.sampling_default: Use simple random sampling and a survey calculator with a confidence level of 90-95% and a confidence interval (margin of error) of 5-10%. Use stratified sampling when there are distinct recipient groups.

indicators.title_template: % of emergency shelters occupied by intended project participants within {occupancy_window} of hand-over

locked.purpose: To measure the results and success of emergency shelter programming by understanding occupancy rates. If a large majority or all participants who received the temporary shelters are occupying them, this indicates the intervention was timely and relevant to the people identified for the assistance.
locked.definition: 'Emergency shelters' are shelters distributed by NRC which meet the minimum standards for temporary shelter set by the CO (or clusters) in terms of habitability (e.g. protected from the elements, provide privacy, a space for sleeping) and align with Sphere standards. 'Occupied' means the temporary shelter is being lived in permanently - i.e. the participant household is living in the shelter all or most days of the week (akin to permanent residence), rather than sporadically or not at all.

calculation.numerator: Number of shelters, meeting the agreed quality requirements, permanently occupied by the recipients who received them, within the allotted time after distribution.
calculation.denominator: Total number of shelters surveyed during the data collection.
calculation.counting_rule: A shelter counts toward the numerator only if, during observation and interview with the main intended occupant, ALL of: (location = same OR suitable other location) AND (quality = excellent OR good) AND (occupied by original recipient, alone or with others).

locked.min_disaggregation: None required. Highly recommended that the CO understands occupancy by sex, displacement status and age groups (and other context factors), but there is no required disaggregation of the shelter unit.
locked.data_source: Person responsible for the shelter within the household.
locked.methodology: Interview with the household representative / person responsible for the shelter, including observation of the shelter.
locked.triangulation: Community-representative KII to corroborate the observation and survey findings - who is occupying the temporary shelters, whether they are the original intended recipients, the general state and utility of the shelters, and inhabitant satisfaction.
locked.analysis: If the indicator meets or exceeds the target, the intervention was well designed, delivered at the right time to the right people, and of the right quality and expectation - i.e. the shelter matched the need. If below target, one or more of: the shelter was not provided at the right time; was not the right quality; did not meet the need/choice of recipients; or the wrong households were identified.
locked.limitations: Does not indicate whether the shelter is relevant and sufficient to meet the needs, choices and preferences of occupants - only that shelters are occupied at the time of visit. Use suggested indicators or qualitative data to assess adequacy.

parameters.label: Occupancy measurement window
parameters.guidance: Decide how long after the provision of a full shelter / shelter support you want to measure occupancy, based on what is feasible and would represent a reasonable outcome in your context. One month is a proposal.

parameters.label: Minimum shelter quality standards (habitability)
fixed_items: Physical safety of the temporary shelter - location
parameters.guidance: These are the standards a shelter must visibly meet to be judged 'good' or 'excellent' quality. The four base standards align with Sphere; add CO-specific standards relevant to your context. This list flows directly into the observation checklist's quality question.
fixed_item_hints: Q: Is the shelter in a physically safe location (away from hazards, flooding, landslide, proximity to conflict)?
Q: Does the shelter protect occupants from rain, wind, sun, cold and heat (roof, walls, floor intact)?
Q: Does the shelter provide adequate privacy for the household, including a separated sleeping area?
Q: Is there a dedicated area within or directly attached to the shelter where occupants can sleep safely?

parameters.label: Occupancy counting conditions (non-original / cohabiting occupants)
parameters.guidance: Specify under which conditions a shelter occupied by someone other than the original recipient can be counted, and whether a shelter counts if the original recipient lives there alongside another household.

parameters.label: Target (% occupancy)
parameters.guidance: Set relatively high, such as 80%. People can be displaced multiple times, especially in the first 6 months of a crisis.

parameters.label: Disaggregation to apply
parameters.guidance: No disaggregation of the shelter unit is required, but disaggregating the occupant profile is highly recommended.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence level (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 90-95%, depending on resources.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence interval / margin of error (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 5-10%, depending on resources.

parameters.label: Sample frame (total emergency shelters distributed this round)
parameters.guidance: The total number of temporary shelters distributed, used to compute the required sample size.

observation_interview.respondent: Person responsible for the shelter within the household
observation_interview.intro: Enumerator instruction: complete by direct observation of the shelter and interview with the main intended occupant. Record one form per surveyed shelter.

questions.name: occupied
questions.label: Is the shelter occupied?
questions.construct: Is the temporary shelter being permanently occupied — lived in all or most days of the week as a principal residence — and by whom?

questions.name: occupant_followup
questions.label: If occupied by a non-original recipient or empty: how was the shelter acquired, who is the head of household, how many people (incl. children, elderly, persons with disability), what is their displacement profile, and do you know where the original recipients are and why they left?
questions.relevant_note: Ask if occupied = not_original or empty.
questions.construct: What is the profile and circumstances of households occupying the shelter who are not the original intended recipients, and what happened to the original recipients?

questions.name: satisfaction
questions.label: How satisfied are you with the temporary shelter?
questions.construct: How satisfied is the respondent household with the temporary shelter they received from NRC?

questions.name: satisfaction_why
questions.label: Why do you give that rating? (tick all that apply)
questions.construct: What specific aspects of the temporary shelter explain the household level of satisfaction or dissatisfaction?

observation_interview.numerator_rule_text: Count this shelter toward the indicator only if: (location = a or b) AND (quality = excellent or good) AND (occupied = a or b).

kii_guide.purpose: Corroborate occupancy findings and locate original intended recipients who were not found during observation.

questions.name: kii_missing_why
questions.label: Why did they vacate / leave the temporary shelter? Provide the stated or suspected reasons, with any relevant context about the household or location.

questions.name: kii_general
questions.label: Other questions pertinent to the CO (general state, utility and satisfaction with the shelters; who is occupying them).

indicators.result: Use of shelter support as intended
indicators.title_template: % of project participants who report / are observed utilizing shelter contribution as intended within {recall_window} of distribution (emergency shelter)

locked.purpose: To validate that the shelter items distributed as part of the shelter contribution were the required ones, distributed in a timely manner and to appropriate households, as indicated by high rates of reported or observed usage of the items as intended. If percentages are low, this means the items were not correctly identified, not given at the right time, or not distributed to the right households — factors that need to be understood.
locked.definition: 'Project participants' are recipients of the temporary shelter contribution who should be found utilizing the temporary shelter contribution at the time of data collection. 'Report/are observed' means the designated HH respondent either confirms the existence of items and their respective usage, or that existence and correct usage of distributed items is observed by the NRC data collector. 'Shelter contribution' means one or several shelter items provided by NRC specifically to the identified household for shelter assistance. 'Utilising as intended' means items are present within the recipient HH and/or being used for their intended purpose (versus traded, lost, or sold). Each CO must decide what percentage of the distributed items must be in use at the time of data collection for the household to be counted.

calculation.numerator: Number of respondents that confirm usage of shelter items for their intended purpose, and/or respondents where usage for intended purpose was confirmed through observation, within the defined period.
calculation.denominator: Total number of households observed/surveyed, as represented by the person interviewed on behalf of each household.
calculation.counting_rule: Count this household only if: for {kit_utilisation_threshold}% or more of the distributed items — (item present = Yes) AND (proper use = Using as intended OR Being used for something else).

locked.min_disaggregation: Sex of respondent (required). Displacement status of respondent (recommended).
locked.data_source: Person who is responsible for the shelter within the household.
locked.methodology: Interview with the HH representative / person responsible for the household, including observation of the shelter support materials.
locked.triangulation: Findings should be corroborated by qualitative data gathered throughout the project — any household FGDs regarding quality of life and specific shelter items, what the assistance may have led to, or what is lacking. Reference CFM information for complaints or feedback regarding usage of household items. Where possible, the data collector should observe the HH to verify whether self-reported information is accurate or plausible.
locked.analysis: If percentages are consistently high, the distributed items are needed and suited to the purpose. If percentages are considerably below the target — especially at the beginning of a distribution series — the distributions are not well suited to the identified households, and/or the wrong households have been identified; in later rounds, items may no longer be required. Information from this indicator can be analysed alongside other shelter indicators to understand how usage of shelter items is affecting household shelter security.
locked.limitations: This indicator does not indicate whether the shelter support provided has made the shelter wholly or partially relevant and sufficient to meet needs/choices of occupants — merely that the items are being used as intended. Other suggested indicators or qualitative data are required to assess whether recipients' shelter is meeting their needs.

parameters.label: Measurement / recall window
parameters.recommended: As short as feasible to ensure evidence of use is still collectible
parameters.guidance: Decide how long after distribution you expect recipients to make reasonable use of the shelter support materials. One month is a proposal. Set this as short as possible to ensure you can still collect appropriate evidence of use.

parameters.label: Kit utilisation threshold (% of items that must be in use for HH to count)
parameters.guidance: Set the minimum percentage of the distributed shelter items that must be present and in use (or being used for an active purpose) for a household to count toward the numerator. For example, 80% means at least 8 out of 10 items must meet the criteria. This allows for some variation in when items can be used and accounts for household circumstances.

parameters.label: Distributed shelter support items
parameters.guidance: List all shelter support items distributed to households as part of this distribution round (e.g. tarpaulin, rope, nails, wooden poles). These items will appear on the observation checklist and the XLSForm questionnaire. Add items exactly as they appear on the distribution list.

parameters.label: Target (% of HHs utilizing contribution as intended)
parameters.guidance: Set the target high, such as 90% of participant households. If earlier rounds return low percentages, increase confidence levels and include qualitative questions to understand the problem.

parameters.label: Disaggregation to apply
parameters.guidance: Sex of respondent is required. Displacement status is recommended. Add other disaggregation relevant to your CO context.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence level (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 90-95%. If earlier rounds return low percentages, use 95% for the next rounds.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence interval / margin of error (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 5-10%. If earlier rounds return low percentages, use 5% (stricter) for the next rounds.

parameters.label: Sample frame (total HHs receiving shelter support this round)
parameters.guidance: The total number of households receiving the shelter contribution in this distribution round. Used to calculate the required sample size.

parameters.label: Stratification groups (if applicable)
parameters.guidance: If you have distinct and different recipient participant groups (e.g. by location, displacement type, shelter type), list them here. Apply the confidence level and interval to each sub-group separately, then add the samples together.

indicators.result: Use of shelter support as intended
indicators.title_template: % of project participants who report / are observed using items purchased with cash as intended within {recall_window} of distribution (emergency shelter)

locked.purpose: To validate that the CVA has been used as intended, and whether it is likely to be a contribution towards people having adequate temporary shelter. High usage rates indicate the CVA was well-targeted, timely, and appropriate. Low rates mean CVA was not utilised as planned — reasons need to be understood.
locked.definition: 'Project participants' are individuals who received CVA to purchase their required shelter items. 'Report/are observed' means the designated respondent either confirms the spend of CVA and the existence and usage of items, or that existence and correct usage of items purchased with NRC CVA is directly observed by the data collector. 'Using items purchased with cash as intended' means: (1) at least the agreed threshold (%) of the total CVA value was spent on shelter items agreed with participants before distribution; (2) the items are present in the household; and (3) the items are being used for what they are designed for. CVA spent on items not part of the initial agreement or on services outside the programme scope is considered not used for the intended purpose.

calculation.numerator: Number of respondents that confirm usage of the agreed majority of CVA for shelter items, and that the items are being used as designed.
calculation.denominator: Total number of households surveyed or observed during the data collection round.
calculation.counting_rule: Count this household only if: (CVA spent on agreed shelter items ≥ {cva_spend_threshold}% of total CVA value) AND for the majority of items observed — (item present = Yes) AND (proper use = Using as intended OR Being used for an active purpose).

locked.min_disaggregation: Sex of respondent (required). Displacement status of household (recommended).
locked.data_source: Person who is responsible for the shelter within the household.
locked.methodology: Interview with the HH representative / the person responsible for the shelter, potentially including observation of the items purchased with CVA.
locked.frequency: Once per distribution round, or once per distribution series if resources are restricted.
locked.triangulation: If vouchers were distributed and NRC has agreements with local vendors, reconciliation of vouchers received by verified vendors should occur. Findings should be corroborated by qualitative data gathered throughout the project — FGDs regarding quality of life and shelter items, what the assistance led to, or what is lacking. Reference CFM information for complaints or feedback. As far as possible, the data collector should observe the HH to verify self-reported information.
locked.analysis: If percentages are high through distribution rounds, CVA was correctly identified and the items work toward meeting an identified shelter need. If percentages are below target, distributions are not well suited to households, or the wrong households were identified (earlier rounds), or items are no longer required (later rounds). Low percentages may also mean CVA was used for other more pressing needs — understand reasons before adjusting the programme.
locked.limitations: This indicator does not indicate whether the items attained through CVA have made the shelter wholly or partially relevant and sufficient to meet needs/choices of occupants — merely that the cash was spent on the agreed items. Other indicators or qualitative data are required to assess whether recipients' shelter meets their needs and preferences.

parameters.label: Measurement / recall window
parameters.recommended: As short as feasible to ensure evidence of CVA use is still collectible
parameters.guidance: Decide how long after CVA distribution you expect recipients to have made reasonable use of the cash. One month is a proposal. Set this as short as possible to ensure you can still collect appropriate evidence of CVA use.

parameters.label: CVA spend threshold (% of total CVA value that must be spent on agreed items for HH to count)
parameters.guidance: Set the minimum percentage of the total cash/voucher value that must have been spent on agreed shelter items for a household to count toward the numerator. Set this high, such as 90%, depending on programmatic and contextual factors.

parameters.label: Agreed shelter items (items participants agreed to purchase with CVA)
parameters.guidance: List the shelter items that were agreed with participants before CVA was distributed. These will appear on the observation checklist and questionnaire. The interviewer will list all items the respondent reports purchasing with CVA and observe whether they are present and in use.

parameters.label: Large CVA volume threshold (no. of HHs above which full Cochran sampling applies)
parameters.guidance: If providing CVA to more than this number of HHs, apply full Cochran sampling (confidence level + interval). If below this threshold, selecting 10-15% of total recipients with simple random sampling is acceptable — adjust based on CO context and resources.

parameters.label: Target (% of HHs using CVA as intended)
parameters.guidance: Set a high target, such as 90% of participant households.

parameters.label: Disaggregation to apply
parameters.guidance: Sex of respondent is required. Displacement status of the household is recommended.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence level (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 90-95%. Apply to each sub-group separately if using stratified sampling.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence interval / margin of error (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 5-10%. If earlier rounds return low percentages, use 5% for subsequent rounds.

parameters.label: Sample frame (total HHs receiving CVA this round)
parameters.guidance: The total number of households receiving CVA in this distribution round. Used to calculate the required sample size.

indicators.result: Use of household items as intended
indicators.title_template: % of participant households who report / are observed using essential household items as intended within {recall_window} of provision (emergency shelter)

locked.purpose: To validate that the essential household items distributed were the required ones, provided in a timely manner and to appropriate households, as indicated by high rates of reported or observed usage of the items as intended. If percentages are low, the items were not correctly identified, not given at the right time, or not distributed to the right households — factors that need to be understood before future distributions.
locked.definition: 'Participant households' are individuals who received essential household items through NRC distribution. 'Report/observed' means the designated HH respondent either confirms the existence of items and their respective usage, or that existence and correct usage is observed by the NRC data collector. 'Used as intended' means the household items distributed are present in the house and being used for what they are intended. The programme team must decide what percentage of items in the kit must have been used by the time of data collection for the kit to be considered as being used.

calculation.numerator: Number of households using the essential household items as intended (the required percentage of items in a kit), within the defined period of time.
calculation.denominator: Total number of households surveyed during the data collection.
calculation.counting_rule: Count this household only if: for {kit_utilisation_threshold}% or more of the distributed household items — (item present = Yes) AND (proper use = Using as intended OR Being used for something else).

locked.min_disaggregation: Sex of head of household (required). Displacement status of household (recommended).
locked.data_source: Person responsible for the shelter within the household, including receipt and management of essential household items.
locked.methodology: Interview with the HH representative / the person responsible for the shelter, potentially including observation of the essential household items.
locked.frequency: Once per distribution round, or once per distribution series if resources are restricted.
locked.triangulation: Conduct an observation of the HH for the household items and their usage wherever possible. Findings should be corroborated by qualitative data gathered throughout the project. Reference CFM information for complaints regarding usage of household items.
locked.analysis: If the percentage meets or exceeds the target, the household items distributed were needed, administered at the right time to the right households, and were of the right quality for the recipients. If below target, the items were not correct, not provided at the right time, not of required quality, or wrong households were identified. Conduct qualitative follow-up to understand the reasons and adjust the programme.
locked.limitations: This indicator provides information on appropriateness and usage of household items at a specific point in time. It does not indicate whether items contributed toward meeting essential household needs overall, or over a longer period during the initial displacement phase.

parameters.label: Measurement / recall window
parameters.recommended: As short as feasible to ensure evidence of use is still collectible
parameters.guidance: Decide how long after distribution you expect recipients to make reasonable use of the household items. One month is a proposal. Set this as short as possible to ensure you can still collect appropriate evidence.

parameters.label: Kit utilisation threshold (% of items that must be in use for HH to count)
parameters.guidance: Set the minimum percentage of the distributed household items that must be present and in use for a household to count toward the numerator. 80% allows for variation in timing of use (e.g. a tarpaulin may not be hoisted if rain hasn't started yet).

parameters.label: Distributed essential household items
parameters.guidance: List all essential household items (NFIs) distributed in this round (e.g. kitchen set, bedding, mosquito net, jerry can). These items will appear on the observation checklist and XLSForm questionnaire.

parameters.label: Target (% of HHs using items as intended)
parameters.guidance: It is recommended to set the target at least 75%. This is not set too high as items may be used at a later stage, and targeting at this point in a response is broad.

parameters.label: Disaggregation to apply
parameters.guidance: Sex of head of household is required. Displacement status of household is recommended.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence level (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 90-95%. If earlier rounds return low percentages, increase to 95% for subsequent rounds.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence interval / margin of error (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 5-10%. If earlier rounds return low percentages, reduce to 5% for subsequent rounds.

parameters.label: Sample frame (total HHs receiving household items this round)
parameters.guidance: The total number of households receiving essential household items in this distribution round.

parameters.label: Stratification groups (if applicable)
parameters.guidance: If you have distinct recipient groups, list them here. Apply confidence level and interval to each sub-group and add samples for the total.

indicators.result: Use of household items as intended
indicators.title_template: % of participant households who report / are observed using items purchased with cash for essential household items as intended within {recall_window} of distribution (emergency shelter)

locked.purpose: To validate that CVA distributed for essential household items was used to purchase the required items in a timely manner and to appropriate households. High rates indicate the intervention was correctly identified and implemented. Low rates mean CVA was not utilised as planned — reasons need to be investigated before new distribution rounds.
locked.definition: 'Participant households' are individuals who received CVA for the purchase of essential household items. 'Report/are observed' means the designated HH respondent either confirms CVA spend and existence and usage of items, or that existence and correct usage of items purchased with CVA is directly observed by the data collector. 'Used as intended' means cash/vouchers were spent to purchase agreed essential household items, and at least the agreed threshold (%) of the total CVA value was spent on these items. The CO must decide this threshold — 75% is a recommendation. At the time of data collection, the items should be present and in use.

calculation.numerator: Number of households who report / are observed to have utilised the agreed threshold (%) of total CVA value for purchase of essential household items, within the defined period of receipt of CVA.
calculation.denominator: Total number of households interviewed during this data collection.
calculation.counting_rule: Count this household only if: (CVA spent on agreed household items ≥ {cva_spend_threshold}% of total CVA value) AND corroborated by observation — for the majority of items: (item present = Yes) AND (proper use = Using as intended OR Being used for an active purpose).

locked.min_disaggregation: Sex of head of household (required). Displacement status of household (recommended).
locked.data_source: Primary person responsible for household expenditure.
locked.methodology: Interview with the HH representative / the person responsible for the shelter, potentially including observation of the items purchased with CVA.
locked.triangulation: If NRC has agreements with local vendors, reconciliation of cash/vouchers received and items purchased should occur. Reference any CFM information. Findings should be corroborated by qualitative data gathered through the project.
locked.analysis: If percentages meet the target, the intervention was correctly identified and implemented. If not, distributions are not well suited to the identified households, or the wrong households were identified, or the timing/quantity/process was inadequate. Low percentages may also indicate CVA was used for other more pressing needs — investigate reasons before adjusting the programme.
locked.limitations: The indicator focuses on ensuring households utilise CVA for essential household items. Information on whether and how these items contributed toward meeting essential household needs overall, over a longer period during the initial displacement phase, is not evident from this indicator alone.

parameters.label: Measurement / recall window
parameters.recommended: As short as feasible to ensure evidence of CVA use is still collectible
parameters.guidance: Decide how long after CVA distribution you expect recipients to have spent the CVA on household items. One month is a proposal. Set this as short as possible.

parameters.label: CVA spend threshold (% of total CVA value that must be spent on agreed items for HH to count)
parameters.guidance: Set the minimum percentage of total CVA value that must have been spent on agreed essential household items for a household to count. 75% is a recommended starting point — set based on programmatic and contextual factors.

parameters.label: Agreed essential household items (items participants agreed to purchase with CVA)
parameters.guidance: List the essential household items agreed with participants before CVA was distributed. These will appear on the observation checklist and questionnaire. The interviewer will list all items the respondent reports purchasing with CVA.

parameters.label: Large CVA volume threshold (no. of HHs above which full Cochran sampling applies)
parameters.guidance: If providing CVA to more than this number of HHs, apply full Cochran sampling. If below this threshold, selecting 10-15% of total recipients with simple random sampling is acceptable.

parameters.label: Target (% of HHs using CVA for household items as intended)
parameters.guidance: Set a high target, such as 90% of participant households.

parameters.label: Disaggregation to apply
parameters.guidance: Sex of head of household is required. Displacement status is recommended.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence level (%)
parameters.guidance: Use 90-95%. Apply to each sub-group separately if using stratified sampling.

parameters.label: Sampling confidence interval / margin of error (%)
